fields.description: Whether the effect is applied when the ability hits. Most effects want this true; setting it false is how an effect is made to trigger only on a miss.
Whether the effect is applied even when the ability misses.
Percentage chance the effect applies at all, rolled per target. 0 behaves as "always", since the roll is only made when a chance is set.
Whether the effect is applied to the world (tiles, cover, environment) on a hit, rather than to a unit. Used by fire, smoke, acid and the other world effects.
As ApplyToWorldOnHit, but for a miss. Grenades typically set both, so they still affect the ground when they scatter.
Records the source player on the effect when it is applied, so later logic can tell whose effect it was. Needed by effects that behave differently for XCOM and the AI.
Marks the effect as impairing the unit, which fires the impairment event and makes the unit report as impaired. This is what stuns, panic and disorientation use.
Fires the impairment event without leaving the unit flagged as impaired afterwards. For effects that interrupt an action but do not linger.
Moves this effect's removal visualization earlier in the sequence, taking the whole context's visualization with it. Used when a removal must be seen before what follows.
Shows a flyover when the target is immune to this effect. Only when the application actually failed because of immunity.
Shows the immunity flyover whenever the effect fails to apply for any reason, not only immunity. Broader, and noisier, than ShowImmunity.
Marks the effect as dealing damage, so it counts towards damage statistics and raises the generic ability-damage events. Set it on any custom source of damage.
Whether the effect is eligible to be redirected onto another target, by Untouchable, Bladestorm parries and similar. Leave false for effects that must hit their target.
Suppresses the usual death message when this effect is what kills the unit, for deaths that should read as something other than a normal kill.
For effects resolved by a stat contest: the contest result must be at least this for the effect to apply. Used to band outcomes, so a stronger roll applies a stronger effect.
Upper bound of the same stat-contest band. Ignored when it is below MinStatContestResult.
Seconds to delay this effect's visualization, for sequencing it against the rest of the ability rather than changing any game state.
Replaces the usual "Miss" flyover with your own text, for abilities where a miss should read as something else.
Damage types this effect counts as. A unit immune to any type listed here resists the effect, and cleansing effects look at these types to decide what they can remove.
Conditions attached to the effect (X2Effect.TargetConditions)
Subtract the per-ruler freeze modifier from the rolled ruler freeze count.
Turns a large unit, an Avatar or a Chosen stays frozen.
Turns any other non-ruler unit stays frozen.
Lower bound of the XCOM actions a ruler stays frozen for. The roll is Rand(Max - Min) + Min.
Upper bound of the ruler freeze roll, exclusive: Min equal to Max gives exactly Min actions.
Re-apply the stat changes when the effect is refreshed. Community Highlander field.
Stat changes applied while the effect lasts, merged by StatType.
The effect never expires on its own. It then only ends through one of the RemoveWhen... rules below, or by something cleansing it.
Ticks once the moment it is applied, rather than waiting for the turn to come round. Damage-over-time effects use this to hurt immediately.
Ticks after every action the target takes rather than once a turn, where the character template supports it.
When ticking per action, multiplies NumTurns by the actions available per turn, so a "3 turn" effect still lasts roughly three turns.
Removes the effect when whoever applied it dies. Typical for effects sustained by their caster, such as mind control.
Removes the effect when the affected unit dies, rather than leaving it on the body.
Removes the effect as soon as the source takes damage, for concentration-style effects broken by being hit.
Removes the effect when the target loses concealment. Used by effects that only make sense while hidden.
Keeps the effect on the unit after it leaves play, until the mission ends. Needed by effects that must still be read when the mission is scored.
Ticks regardless of whose turn it is. Normally an effect only ticks on its owner’s turn.
Only one target may carry this effect from a given source at a time; applying it elsewhere removes the earlier one.
Re-applying the effect increments a stack counter instead of simply refreshing its duration, so effects that grow with repetition can read the count.
When checking whether the target already has this effect, only consider copies from the same source. Lets several units apply their own instance.
A unit reduced to zero health while under this effect bleeds out instead of dying outright.
Whether the effect appears in the unit’s status UI at all. An effect with no FriendlyName set will show as blank.
Shows FriendlyName in the damage feedback as a distinct source, so its damage reads separately from the weapon’s.
As DisplayInUI, but for the unit that applied the effect rather than the one carrying it.
How many turns the effect lasts. Ignored when InfiniteDuration is true.
Percentage chance the effect is shed immediately on the first tick, before PerTurnShedChance takes over.
Percentage chance per tick that the effect wears off early. 0 means it only ends when its turns run out.
Precedence among effects of the same kind, used by auras so a stronger source wins over a weaker one.
Decides which effect controls the unit’s animation when several apply at once. The higher value wins.
Narrows the unit’s sight arc to this many degrees. When two effects both set it, the smaller arc applies.
Idle animation to play while the effect is active, taking over the unit’s normal idle.
Identifier used when deciding how this effect stacks with others, and the name other effects use to find or remove it.
Which ability this is presented as coming from. Controls how a passive buff is coloured in the HUD.
Event fired when the effect is applied, for listeners and triggered abilities to react to.
Event fired when the per-turn shed-chance roll succeeds.
Socket on the unit’s skeleton to attach the particle system to.
Named array of sockets to attach the particle system to, for effects that appear in several places at once. Optional.
Name shown in the unit’s status UI.
Description shown beneath FriendlyName in the status UI.
Path to the status icon shown in the UI.
Name shown on the unit that applied the effect, as opposed to the one carrying it.
Description shown on the applying unit.
Short label drawn on the applying unit’s icon.
Path to the small status icon used in condensed UI, alongside IconImage.
Particle system played on the unit for as long as the effect lasts.
Perk effect played on the unit while this effect is active.
